4.text:
<C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0004,><C:0001,0001,>～Volume 1～
[Peaceful Island, Folk of Mystery]<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0000,>Soft winds ever blow across Pi'illo Island,
whispering of lore and legend...<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>A strange people once made their home
here, and it is said they were possessed
of a mysterious power.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>What power, you ask, intrepid reader?
The power to slip through the veil that
separates the real and dream worlds.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>These were the Pi'illo folk for whom
this island is named, and under their
care, it was a flourishing paradise.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>But time laughs at mortal works,
and now old ruins dotted about the
island are all that remains.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>What fate befell the inhabitants of
this island? How did their line falter?
Whence came their hidden end?<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Consider these humble writings an
attempt to record all that is known
of the Pi'illos...and their end.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0001,>Continued in Volume 2...
[Prince Dreambert]<C:0003,0001,>

6.text:
<C:0001,0001,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0004,>～Volume 2～
[Prince Dreambert]<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0000,>The Pi'illos were at the peak of their
prominence, and they were led by their
young ruler, Prince Dreambert.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>The youthful leader's crowning 
achievement had been the construction
of Pi'illo Castle, a monumental edifice.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Though cast in stone, the structure
embodied the cultural and artistic
sensibilities of Dreambert's people.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>As any visitor can attest, the castle
still reflects both the prosperity and
the peaceful nature of the Pi'illo prince.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>But it reflects more. For it is said
that somewhere within is a strange
room... A snapshot of Pi'illo culture.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>By sleeping in this room, the legend
claims, one dreams of Pi'illo enemies
and can revel in their defeats.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>The Pi'illos were a tranquil people,
to be sure...but the prince bid all
soldiers hone their skills in this room.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Did young Dreambert have a
premonition of evil times?<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Did he foresee that some fell thing
would one day come with ruin in tow?<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0001,>Continued in Volume 3...
[The Nightmare Begins]<C:0003,0001,>

2.text:
<C:0001,0001,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0004,>～Volume 3～
[The Nightmare Begins]<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0000,>History teaches that time and again,
across the aeons, good will always be
eventually beset by evil.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Evil soon came for Pi'illo Island as well.
An evil born of foul parents. Its mother
was corruption; its father, base cunning.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>It flapped into being and all trembled!
For it was the evil mage-king of bats,
and its name was Antasma.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>None know in what dark den it was
born or what nightmare byways led
it to Pi'illo Island's shores...<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>But once it came to roost on the
island, the fate of the peaceful
inhabitants was set in stone.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Though they knew it not, their
sandy footsteps now trudged down
the path of their own destruction.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0001,>Continued in Volume 4...
[The Two Stones]<C:0003,0001,>

3.text:
<C:0001,0001,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0004,>～Volume 4～
[The Two Stones]<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0000,>Why had the evil Antasma come?
The answer: stones. For the Pi'illos had
ever guarded two precious stones.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>The first was called the Dream Stone.
Embedded within this wondrous stone
was all the power of beautiful dreams.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>There was another: the Dark Stone.
And within this slept all the power 
and danger of the world's nightmares.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Both stones held a terrible strength,
for they could fulfil the desires of
whoever held them.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Antasma looked upon the Dark Stone
with ravenous eyes and decided it
would be his and his alone...<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>By insidious means and black arts,
he spirited the Dark Stone from the
sanctuary where it slept.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>But he would not go unchallenged.
Dreambert discovered the plot and led
many Pi'illos to confront Antasma.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>They surrounded the stolen stone,
but the fiend would not yield, and the
battle was soon joined.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0001,>Continued in Volume 5...
[The Great Battle]<C:0003,0001,>

1.text:
<C:0001,0001,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0004,>～Volume 5～
[The Great Battle]<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0000,>The Pi'illos were fundamentally a
peaceful people, and they held to this
tenet as best they could.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>However, with their land and culture
held hostage, their fury grew terrible
and they fought without mercy.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>At Prince Dreambert's command,
the Pi'illos hurled themselves into the
fray in an all-out attack on Antasma.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>None would permit Antasma's dark
designs to come to fruition, even if it
meant their own lives were forfeit.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>For all knew that the Dark Stone,
that nightmare in crystalline form,
must never be used.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Yet even when the battle went ill,
no spirit quailed, for the Pi'illos knew
they had a powerful ally.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>The power of this ally was without
equal. And it stood with the Pi'illos.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>It was the Zeekeeper.
The bird of legend.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0001,>Continued in Volume 6...
[The Feathered Guardian]<C:0003,0001,>

3.text:
<C:0001,0001,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0004,>～Volume 6～
[The Feathered Guardian]<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0000,>Legend has it that the Zeekeeper was
a bird of enormous girth who watched
over and guarded people's dreams.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>It was massive, draped in iridescent
feathers, and terrifying when roused
in defence of the righteous.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>The great bird lived in quiet peace as
it watched over the island dwellers,
but in battle, it was dire.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>From its mind's eye, the Zeekeeper
could launch a Wakebeam, a weapon
of unimaginable power versus evil.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>This weapon bedevilled Antasma in
battle to the point of despair.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>And so, with the help of their mighty
ally, it looked as though the Pi'illos 
would prove the victors at long last.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>As he looked upon the field of battle,
Prince Dreambert awaited his chance
to execute one final manoeuvre.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Little did he know, however, that his
plan would lead to utter ruin.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0001,>Continued in Volume 7...
[The Wise One's Gambit]<C:0003,0001,>

5.text:
<C:0001,0001,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0004,>～Volume 7～
[The Wise One's Gambit]<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0000,><C:0001,0004,>As he listened to reports of the battle,
Dreambert mulled over courses of action.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0000,>"How can we do the most good?
We must defeat Antasma, but how can
we ensure this danger never returns?"<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>To answer his question, the prince
called forth one of his subjects.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>It was none other than Eldream.
Long-lived and wise, he knew all there
was about the island and dreams.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Eldream was also the only Pi'illo who
had befriended the animals of the
island, with whom he shared kinship.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Prince Dreambert, in close counsel
with this wise and ancient advisor,
concocted a secret plan.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>The plan was this: to seal Antasma
deep within a dream...forever.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>But could the evil one be eternally
imprisoned in the dark, ethereal pit
known only as Dream's Deep?<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0001,>Continued in Volume 8...
[The Nightmare's Dream]<C:0003,0001,>

7.text:
<C:0001,0001,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0004,>～Author's Postscript～<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0000,>Buh huh huh huh huh! Oh hello, loyal reader!
It is I, Pi'illoper, your humble author and bed
lover, wrecking the fourth wall to add a word!<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>As my imaginary friends know, I have always
had a great passion for the noble Pi'illos, and
it led me to self-publish these little screeds!<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Some might call it fan fiction... I snort at that!
How much fan fiction has TEN volumes? Huh?
Not many, I'd bet. Did you read them all?<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Buh huh huh! Not to toot my own horn here,
but who'd imagine I could write a masterpiece
with such a dearth of historical materials?<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Which reminds me, my imaginary lawyers advise
me to assert that this work is not affiliated
with Pi'illo Castle or any official Pi'illo anything!<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>All this humble author hopes is that you might
read these and gain a greater appreciation for
the Pi'illo folk, be the tales real or imagined!<C:0003,0001,>

4.text:
<C:0001,0001,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0004,>～Volume 8～
[The Nightmare's Dream]<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0000,>The Pi'illo attack continued unabated.
With the Zeekeeper's support, they
brought Antasma to bay.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0000,>At Eldream's bidding, the beasts of
the forests rose up and they, too,
surrounded Antasma.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>So relentless was the assault that
Antasma clasped the Dark Stone
fast to his chest, muting its powers.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>From his vantage, Dreambert saw
this and knew the time had come.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>He would set his last, desperate
plan in motion and attempt to
seal Antasma away forever.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>If it succeeded, Antasma could
never cross the dream border.
Dream's Deep would be his prison.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Such was the course that 
Dreambert and Eldream had 
settled upon in their extremity.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>However, just as the portal to 
the world of dreams yawned open
and Antasma's doom was nigh...<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Something truly terrible happened.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0001,>Continued in Volume 9...
[The Final Struggle]<C:0003,0001,>

6.text:
<C:0001,0001,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0004,>～Volume 9～
[The Final Struggle]<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0000,>Antasma was slowly swallowed by
the closing portal to the dream world,
and Dreambert sensed victory at hand.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0000,>But it was not to be. Catastrophe
loomed, felt first by the creatures of
the forest that Eldream had called.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0000,>They abandoned their circle of
containment around Antasma and began
a frantic retreat.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0000,>Eldream noticed something was amiss.
He opened his mouth to cry out a
warning, but just at that moment...<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>A faint sneer appeared on the lips
of Antasma, hated and accursed.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Using all the terrible strength left
in his vile hands, the mage-king of
bats crushed the Dark Stone.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>His fell body had already been
swallowed by the void...<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Now, last of all, his fist slowly
disappeared, and Antasma was lost
to the depths of the dream world.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0001,>Continued in the final chapter...
[Dream without End]<C:0003,0001,>

8.text:
<C:0001,0001,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0004,>～The Final Chapter～
[Dream without End]<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0000,>The portal to the dream world closed
on Antasma, and the Pi'illos seemed the
victors at last.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>But the Dark Stone had fragmented,
and now nightmare chunks fell from
the sky, shimmering in the darkness.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>The soft bodies of the Pi'illos began
hardening into stone, and one by one
they collapsed onto the grass.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Before long, neither victors nor the
fallen stood on the field of battle.
Only silence remained.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Who knows how much time has
passed since that dark day?<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>None know, but know this last:
When all movement on the plain had
ceased, a single rabbit appeared.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>It bounced like a stone in the surf
and then seemed to find a Pi'illo it
knew from among the fallen many.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Then, as if to protect the Pi'illo,
the rabbit lay against the stone,
closed its eyes, and slept.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>From then on, nothing marked the
passage of time on the island but
the silence of the stone Pi'illos.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0001,>～The End～

8.text:
<C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0001,><C:0001,0004,>- Here Lies a Hero of Buffness -
Muscle Lord Pullurp<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>Pullurp was the most celebrated of all athletes
who participated in the Ultrapump Games.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>He lifted his body up with such force that
onlookers feared it would crack the firmament.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>He thrust it downwards with such enthusiasm
that he threatened to breach the earth's mantle.<C:0003,0001,><C:0000,0004,><C:0007,0000,>And yet, his lone failure came on the parallel bars,
where the Double Glute Spin eluded him all his life.<C:0003,0001,>

6.text:
<C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0001,>Lured by the wonderful scent,
Mario and Luigi press forward.
Their bodies feel oddly light.
Their legs flex into the earth.
Their moustaches flutter like
gossamer in the mountain breeze.
The smell grows stronger.
They travel for great leagues...
Or do they barely travel at all?
Soon they find the smell's source.

7.text:
<C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0001,>They find endless mushrooms.
An unimaginable mound of mushrooms.

MUSHROOMS!

Mario jumps onto the mushroom pile...
Luigi leaps onto the mushroom pile...
They chew and inhale mushrooms...
They devour as many as they can,
their banquet interrupted by no one.

8.text:
<C:0007,0000,><C:0001,0001,>They know not how much they ate.
A white cloud appears beside Mario.
His gloves caress the atmosphere.
His soaking boots absorb the sea.
Hills shrink... No! The bros are huge!
They have grown as big as the island!
Thousands of times bigger than life!
A finger flick could smash Bowser!
There is nothing for them to fear.
In this moment, they are ecstatic.

Pi'illo Island becomes famous,
and the party never ends.
